result.title: INCISE: Training-Free In-Context Segmentation of Surgical Videos
result.summary: Surgical video analysis requires video object segmentation (VOS), yet existing methods are commonly based on pretrained model fine-tuning using a large number of expert labels. In-context segmentation (ICS) offers the promise of bypassing this high cost by segmenting a target video using a few annotated references, which are the sole source of surgical knowledge for a frozen model. However, existing ICS methods tend to draw such references at random, which concentrate on a few views that dominate a surgical video and can miss other objects of interest (e.g., transient instruments and small structures). To address these challenges, we propose INCISE, a training-free ICS framework for surgical videos. INCISE selects unlabeled frames from multiple surgical videos that jointly cover the local appearances of a target video, and then segments the target video using these references. With only 1.7% of training frames selected and annotated as references and no target video frame labeled, INCISE obtains 67.2% mean mIoU and outperforms the best SOTA fine-tuned method by 9.2 points. We hope INCISE can help establish ICS as a practical alternative to fine-tuning in surgical video analysis and other domains with a costly labeling burden.

AI.brief_summary: 面向手术视频的免训练上下文分割框架：从多段视频中挑选能覆盖目标视频局部外观的未标注帧作为参考标注，再用冻结模型分割目标视频，以极少参考帧超过微调 SOTA。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按外观覆盖度选取少量参考帧的思路，可能与 LVR 中预算受限的视觉证据筛选与采样策略有概念联系，但该文不涉及推理状态或答案生成，可供核查的借鉴较为间接。
